system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Page counts (en 3, ar 6) are within the 15-page maximum, and the encodings are appropriate (GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic). Neither language tells people what to do, so the first page cannot carry the action. The two versions also give different end times (19:00 in English, 21:00 in Arabic).

objections.issue: No protective action appears in either language, so the first page carries the hazard but no action. In Arabic (41 characters a page) the first page also only reaches 'winds'; dust and sand and reduced visibility fall onto page 2.
objections.fix: Add a short protective action at the start of both texts, for example: Drive carefully, keep your distance and avoid unnecessary travel; people with breathing problems should stay indoors. Restructure the Arabic so the first 41 characters name the dust or sand hazard and the action, for example: غبار ورمال وتدني الرؤية: قد بحذر وتجنب السفر غير الضروري. Keep both languages within 15 pages.

evidence.quote: coupled with a description of the threat and the protective action the public should take
Fresh to strong northwesterly winds are blowing dust and sand, cutting visibility to under 2,000 metres

objections.issue: The two language versions conflict on when the alert expires. English says 'until 19:00 this evening' and Arabic says 'حتى الساعة 21:00'. Recipients reading different languages would get different information.
objections.fix: Confirm the correct end time against the National Centre of Meteorology source. Make the English and Arabic texts state the same time.
